issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal and its concrete subclasses: the template Main (example usage) and the problem statement imply single-argument constructors that accept only the animal name (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). Specifically, Template Main instantiates Seal, Pig, and Goat using a single String argument (lines show new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")). In the solution, Animal and all concrete subclasses provide two-parameter constructors requiring (String name, int age) (e.g., Animal(String name, int age); Seal(String name, int age); Pig(String name, int age); Goat(String name, int age)). This mismatch will cause students following the provided Main/example to get compilation errors or to implement constructors incompatible with the solution reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) remove the additional 'age' parameter from the solution so Animal and subclasses have single-argument constructors (e.g., public Animal(String name) and public Seal(String name)), and adjust solution code/tests accordingly; or (B) update the problem statement and the template Main to require and demonstrate two-argument constructors (String name, int age) for Animal and subclasses (update UML, textual description, and Main instantiation calls). Apply the chosen option consistently to Animal and all subclasses.

issues.description: Attribute set mismatch for class Animal: the problem statement/UML specifies Animal has a single attribute 'name: String' (UML lines show name: String), whereas the solution's Animal class defines an extra attribute 'age' (private int age) in addition to 'name'. The presence of this extra attribute in the solution changes required state and constructor requirements and is not documented in the problem statement or template, which can confuse students about which fields to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the attribute lists consistent. Either: (A) remove the 'age' field and its getters/setters from the solution so Animal only contains 'name: String' and adjust constructors to a single name parameter; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to include 'age: int' as an explicit attribute and update the template Main and any examples to show the two-argument constructors and explain the additional attribute. Document the chosen attribute set clearly in the problem text and UML.
